Headline

All four files now pass check_file with no banned words and no long sentences. The procedure in notes/procedure.md guided the fixes in the order requested. Notes a.md, b.md, and c.md keep their original meaning.

Background

The request asked for a reusable procedure file first, then fixes to three notes files. The sandbox check_file tool reports banned words and sentences over 25 words.

Relevance

A working procedure lets any agent repeat these fixes. Verified clean files remove blocker words and long sentences.

Information

Fixes applied per file:

- notes/a.md: removed the booster "clearly" [1].
- notes/b.md: split one 38 word sentence into three short sentences and kept all facts [1].
- notes/c.md: removed the booster "very" and split one 35 word sentence into four short sentences [1].

The check after the writes reported zero failures for all four files [1].

Alternative considered: rewrite the notes in full. It loses because small edits preserve the original meaning at lower risk.

End

I recommend that we follow these steps next:

1. Read notes/procedure.md before any further edits. Domain: Clear, because the steps follow a known rule. Test: Given a notes file with banned words, When the agent follows steps 1 to 8, Then check_file reports zero failures.
2. Re-run check_file on any notes file that changes. This removes the blocker of quiet regressions. Domain: Clear, because the tool gives a fixed pass rule. Test: Given an edited file, When check_file runs, Then it reports zero banned words and zero long sentences.

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences in one notes file

Tools: read_file, check_file, write_file. Run this procedure on one file at a time.

1. Run check_file on the target file. Note the banned words and the sentences over 25 words that it reports.
2. Run read_file on the target file.
3. Remove or replace each banned word. Replace it only when a replacement keeps the meaning. Otherwise delete it.
4. Split each sentence over 25 words into two or more sentences. Keep every fact. Do not change the order of events.
5. Keep the title and the structure of the file. Do not add new content.
6. Run write_file to save the revised text in full.
7. Run check_file again on the file. Confirm it reports no banned words and no sentences over 25 words.
8. If check_file still reports problems, go back to step 3. Otherwise the file is done.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service fell back to the database for every request. This continued until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. It writes the result to the store. Then it marks the message as done so that no other worker picks it up again.
